name: Newegg Refreshed (first-party refurbished) Intel Arc B580 12GB tier
price_basis: REFURBISHED via Newegg's own 'Newegg Refreshed' tier, bare PCIe consumer card. $199.99 = ONIX ODYSSEY B580 12GB, and also the Intel Arc B580 Limited Edition. Other refreshed asks: ASRock Challenger B580 $259.99, Acer Nitro B580 $249.99. Captured 2026-10-03. For comparison the same page shows NEW ASRock Challenger B580 at $329.99 (list $355.15) and NEW Intel B580 Limited Edition at $590.00. Warranty: Newegg Refreshed carries its own programme warranty, distinct from and shorter than a full manufacturer warranty - the exact term was not published in the extracted page PERISHABLE-FIGURE STAMP (added 2026-10-04, uniform across data/supply/ so it is greppable). PRICE CLASS: ASKING price captured from a live listing or product page - the price at which a seller advertises the item right now. NOT a sold/completed transaction price, NOT an auction result and NOT a dealer cost; for used or refurbished parts the gap between ask and realised is typically wide. OBSERVED: 2026-10-03 RE-VERIFY BY: 2027-01-04 - the repo's quarterly re-verification bar. After that date this figure is presumed drifted and must be re-checked against its source before it is quoted again. A price without its observation date is noise; this stamp exists so a reader can tell a fresh figure from a stale one without reading prose. UNIT: REFURBISHED via Newegg's own 'Newegg Refreshed' tier, bare PCIe consumer card READING RULE: No further perishable flag is published for this figure.
notes:
The only first-party refurb channel in this slice that publishes live prices for consumer accelerators, and the contrast with eBay used is the point: refreshed $199.99-$259.99 versus used $290.00-$499.00 versus new $329.99-$590.00. Buying USED Intel silicon is strictly dominated - the refurbished tier is 27% to 34% below new and 31% to 55% below used. That ordering (refurb < used < new) is the opposite of what most people assume, and it holds because used consumer cards here are thin supply with no warranty while the refurb tier is a steady pipeline. AVAILABILITY CAVEAT, important: every refreshed unit in the captured listing was marked OUT OF STOCK. Newegg Refreshed on B580 is a browse-able but rarely actually purchasable tier - treat these as achievable prices, not as items in stock today. This also means availability is recorded as unknown rather than in-stock despite prices showing.

 LEAD TIME: null, and deliberately so. A marketplace or big-box reseller publishes STOCK STATE, not a lead time - where this record shows in-stock that means the listing was available on the observation date, and where it shows backorder no week window is published at all. Converting one into the other would be an invention. The one exception in the whole chain is CDW, which does print windows (source spl-cdw-published-lead-times-gpu-2026-10); note that even there the scarcest SKUs - the RTX PRO 6000 96GB cards and DGX Spark - read 'Item Backordered' with NO estimate, so scarcity and lead time are inversely related in what distributors actually publish. Probe log in source spl-negative-no-oem-publishes-lead-time.

 EXPORT CONTROL (2026-10-04, mechanism-level; source spl-eccn-3a090-ccl): this is a CONSUMER discrete board (Intel Arc B580 class), which does not meet the ECCN 3A090.a 'total processing performance' >= 4800 or TPP >= 1600 / performance density >= 5.92 thresholds, so it is not an advanced-computing item and the case-by-case / D:5 licence regime does not attach to it; consumer parts of this class generally sit under ECCN 3A001 or are designated EAR99. Recorded FALSE for that reason, NOT because the part is unregulated - it remains under the EAR, subject to destination-country import rules and to screening of the consignee and its ultimate parent against the Entity, Unverified and MEU lists under 15 CFR part 744. This is the case that makes the point sharpest: an Intel Arc B580 and a datacentre accelerator can be sold by the same distributor on the same day under completely different regimes, so export status has to be recorded per part rather than inferred from vendor or channel.
export_control_regime: EAR 3A001 or EAR99 (below the 3A090.a TPP / performance-density thresholds) + EAR 744.23 (Entity List) + EAR 744.6 (Unverified / MEU lists)
export_control_note: MECHANISM: the part falls BELOW the ECCN 3A090.a/.b TPP and performance-density thresholds, so the advanced-computing licence regime, its case-by-case China/Macau carve-out and its D:5 screening do NOT attach. What remains is the general EAR plus destination-country import rules and screening of the consignee and its ultimate parent against the Entity, Unverified and MEU lists. NO LICENCE REQUIRED for the sale itself; the screening is a party-listing check, not a performance-threshold check. The binding ECCN determination for any specific part is the exporter's own classification, not this record.
lead_time_basis: NEGATIVE, DELIBERATELY NOT STRUCTURAL: no lead time in weeks is printed for these SKUs. It is not that no vendor in the chain publishes one - CDW does, and it is recorded on cdw-enterprise as 'published' - but this channel routes to 'request a quote' or shows a stock count instead, so the number exists elsewhere in the market and is not surfaced here. Checked 2026-10-04 per source spl-negative-no-oem-publishes-lead-time.
